light.note: r26: the window aperture re-derived FOR ITS CORRECTED AIM. Its 38 W was set while it fired into a wall 15 mm away, so almost none of it reached the room except as bounce off that patch; facing the room it is a different source. Bracketed 22/45/80 W at a held key: SHAPE 0.3664 / 0.2515 / 0.2570. Both then scaled 0.8272 to put the FULL frame on the target p50 — SHAPE is exposure-independent so the bracket verdict survives the scaling.

declared_gaps.duvet: RETURNED r17 as the lane's first simulated cloth (was: removed after R1 stop-loss as a hand-modelled box, which R8 forbids). The class distinction that licenses this: what failed in TRN-001 was closed-tube pinned garments; a duvet is an open flat sheet on rigid colliders, the solver's proven class (PRJ-2026-002 folded_sheet hotel roll, every simulated bed cloth passed the owner's eye there). Recipe inherited whole from that lane; feedstock footprint here is MEASURED from the target through the solved camera.
declared_gaps.lamp_stem: REMOVED (audit + owner's own catch). A bare post whose provenance read 'carries shade'. The audit measured hard containment for the lamp: no pixel may fall left of u=1057, and the stem projects to u 1061-1075 with nothing like it in the reference. The shade is retained; what held it up was invented. R10.
declared_gaps.shelf_col_base: REMOVED (audit). An 818 mm plinth under the etagere that is 100% occluded in BOTH frames, invented so the boards would have something beneath them - the lamp_stem pattern exactly. Its own prov quoted 'top z~3030', a number belonging to the COLUMN, pasted onto a base whose top is 818. The carcass now runs continuously from the worktop, which is what the reference shows.
declared_gaps.artwork_relief: The target's print is an embossed letterform panel. Not built - a styling-round ticket. What r14 does build is the FRAME, because the artwork's own `seen` line measured a 21 mm black bar at luma 28-33 against a 175-187 wall (a 6:1 contrast) and the mass had been wearing a 0.78-albedo white the whole time. Measured and never built is its own defect class, and this frame and the door's shadow gaps are both instances of it.
declared_gaps.blind_slats: BUILT and measured (pitch 29.4 mm from 89 peaks in the target's own column; extent confirmed twice against the light rig's independent backprojection) but WITHDRAWN from the frame. With the aperture modelled as an emitting card 35 mm behind the slats, every GAP shows the emitter — so a gap is the brightest thing in the band instead of the darkest, and the band renders at 0.445 against the target's 0.250 with only +0.145 of periodicity against the target's +0.517. Power and tilt were both bracketed and neither is the knob: at 8/16/22 W the band/wall ratio runs 1.44/1.89/2.17 against a target of 0.80, and extrapolating to ZERO aperture power still lands at 0.89. The slats need the window modelled as a glazing plane with a source BEYOND it, which is a round of its own. The generator and its 4 tests are kept (trn002_geom.slat_stack, mass kind 'slats').
declared_gaps.right_wall_x: The room's right boundary and the wardrobe's depth are the same unknown after r27. See the right_wall mass.
declared_gaps.petcave_mouth_depth: 450 mm, declared. Nothing in this frame sees into the cave far enough to measure how deep it is; what the depth controls is how black the cavity renders, so it is bracketable against the target's 0.0003 rather than guessable.
declared_gaps.closet_oak_depth: The niche's depth is unmeasurable from this camera — its floor contact is behind the partition's bottom rail. Placed on the closet back wall by declaration; the projected extent is measured and is what the frame is judged on.
declared_gaps.closet_niche_contents: The target's niche carries a warm LED strip at its head, a shirt on a wooden hanger, a shelf with a small box and a pair of glasses. None is built. The shirt is free-form and belongs to ACQUIRE (R8), never to a modelling round.
declared_gaps.partition_glass: The left leaf is glazed in the target — a faint veil and edge highlights over the chair behind it. No glass mass exists and the shader has no transmission channel. Not built this round: the opening had to exist before glass over it could mean anything.
declared_gaps.light_ticket_1: LIGHT TICKET (r32, measured twice from opposite directions): lacquer_white wants k=1.1976 through our own irradiance, which lands its albedo at sRGB 244.7 — past the studio's 240 dielectric ceiling. No repaint can reach it: the target puts more light on this surface than our rig does.
declared_gaps.light_ticket_2: LIGHT TICKET (r32, measured twice from opposite directions): upholstery_bed wants k=1.0825 through our own irradiance, which lands its albedo at sRGB 248.5 — past the studio's 240 dielectric ceiling. No repaint can reach it: the target puts more light on this surface than our rig does.
declared_gaps.light_ticket_3: LIGHT TICKET (r32): paint_white is ONE material on back wall and left wall. The target renders them 1.58x apart and we render them 1.01x apart (LIGHT_SPAN 0.022) — within one material that difference can only be light, and it is the largest material in the room. Our walls do not differ, so the room has no direction in its light.
declared_gaps.texture_paint_white: paint_white reads 1.76-22.21x the target's fine detail depending on WHICH object wears it. A single material cannot be six different amounts wrong, so this is content in the target we do not model — most of it on closet_back, which already stands in for both a wall and a window. Declared here rather than fixed with a relief, because a relief would make the number better and the model worse.

audit_conflicts.bed_width: RESOLVED r16 by the method agreed at r14: fit the platform's own far long side and nothing else. Width = 2075 +/- 40 (near -4180, far -2105+/-20). Both priors die: 1595's anchors were a fabric silhouette that fails the plane test everywhere and a headboard end fitted at the room corner's own pixel column; the audit's 2100 came from an assumed rounded-corner plan and lands 50 mm long. Third constraint closes green: two measured 800 mm pillows need 1640 and the mattress is now 1719.
